item.title: Intune action pages now document tenant-wide daily caps for Wipe, Retire, and Delete — 18 August 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 18 August 2026

Intune action pages now document tenant-wide daily caps for Wipe, Retire, and Delete

The four updates are documentation clarifications to Intune device-action limits, not evidence of a new feature, preview, general-availability change, or retirement. The pages specify cumulative tenant-wide daily ceilings across individual, bulk, and Microsoft Graph submissions.

Intune · General

Wipe is documented at 500 actions per tenant per day

The Wipe page now states that individual device actions, bulk actions, and Microsoft Graph API requests count cumulatively toward a 500-action daily tenant limit. It also documents contacting Microsoft support to request a different limit.

Intune · General

Retire is documented at 1,000 actions per tenant per day

The Retire page now states that individual, bulk, and Microsoft Graph requests count cumulatively toward a 1,000-action daily limit for each tenant. Administrators can contact Microsoft support to request a limit change.

Intune · General

Delete is documented at 1,000 actions, including cascading outcomes

The Delete guidance states that tenants can submit up to 1,000 Delete actions per day across individual actions, bulk actions, and Microsoft Graph requests. The cumulative count includes Deletes that trigger Retire or Wipe.

item.title: Intune sync guidance now covers iOS/iPadOS and multiple Windows workloads — 14 August 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 14 August 2026

Intune sync guidance now covers iOS/iPadOS and multiple Windows workloads

The period is dominated by documentation clarification rather than a feature launch, preview announcement, general availability change, retirement, or confirmed service-behavior change. Sync guidance now describes policy, app, script, and remediation processing, extends the documented scope to iOS/iPadOS as well as Windows, and identifies the Device sync status tab for progress tracking. A separate Android Management API update clarifies the correct reporting location.

Intune · General

Sync guidance adds broader workload and device coverage

The Sync page now states that selecting Sync triggers policy processing, app state updates, and scripts or remediations, with progress available in the Device sync status tab. The documented behavior applies to iOS/iPadOS and Windows devices, and the described improvements require the Preview new device view toggle.

Intune · Windows

Windows guidance documents combined MDM and IME check-ins

The updated Windows Management Extension guidance says that Sync from Windows Settings or the Intune admin center initiates both MDM and IME check-ins, including policy, app, script, and remediation processing. Administrators can view progress in the Device sync status tab.

Intune · Device enrollment

Android Management API reporting location is clarified

Administrators are directed to the Personal Devices on Android Management API report under Devices > Monitor. The update explicitly says this reporting does not appear in the policy’s device assignment status or the device configuration tab.

item.title: Intune plans higher Apple OS floors: iOS 18 and macOS 15 later this year — 13 August 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 13 August 2026

Intune plans higher Apple OS floors: iOS 18 and macOS 15 later this year

Microsoft announced two planned Intune support changes tied to Apple’s next major OS releases. After iOS/iPadOS 27 becomes available, Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or later. After macOS Golden Gate 27 is released, Intune will support macOS 15 and later; existing devices on macOS 14.x or below will remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will be blocked.

Intune · App management

iOS/iPadOS support moves to version 18 or later

After Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27 later this year, Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or higher. Administrators should check device compatibility and Intune reports, including the specific requirements for userless Automated Device Enrollment devices, and use Intune OS-version controls where appropriate.

Intune · Device enrollment

macOS 15 becomes the supported enrollment baseline

After macOS Golden Gate 27 releases later this year, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Existing devices on macOS 14.x or below will remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will no longer be allowed.

item.title: Intune guidance flags registry exposure, approval boundaries, and macOS enrollment risks — 7 August 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 7 August 2026

Intune guidance flags registry exposure, approval boundaries, and macOS enrollment risks

The 7 August period is documentation-heavy: all 32 recorded items are updates, with no new, removed, or Message Center entries. The most consequential changes clarify security exposure, Multi Admin Approval scope, macOS enrollment prerequisites, Microsoft Tunnel installation requirements, and Windows Autopilot network endpoints. The supplied evidence does not establish a new feature launch, general availability change, retirement, or broad product behavior change.

Intune · Windows

Registry inventory data is explicitly identified as sensitive configuration information

The Collect Device Properties guidance now states that collected registry key data is accessible through existing Device Inventory permissions and may expose sensitive device configuration information. This is security and privacy guidance, not evidence that the permission model changed; review access and handling of the collected data.

Intune · Fundamentals

Multi Admin Approval guidance defines delegated and app-authenticated Graph coverage

The guidance now clarifies that MAA applies to delegated actions and app-authenticated Microsoft Graph API calls when policies are configured. Per-policy enterprise application exclusions for app-auth calls are limited to 50 applications, require second-admin approval, and are audited; excluded applications can bypass approval for the affected resource type.

Intune · Device enrollment

Userless macOS ADE devices should not receive PSSO registration profiles

The Automated Device Enrollment guidance warns that targeting userless ADE devices with PSSO configuration profiles that enable PSSO registration during Setup Assistant can cause unexpected enrollment behavior and loss of expected device affinity. Review assignments and exclude those devices.

Intune · Device security

Microsoft Tunnel on RHEL 9.8 requires manual ip_tables loading

The prerequisites now list Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9.8 with Podman 5.8.2 or later as the default. Because RHEL 9.8 does not automatically load the ip_tables kernel module, administrators must load it manually before installing Microsoft Tunnel.

Windows Autopilot · Windows

Windows Autopilot diagnostics guidance replaces regional upload endpoints

The Endpoints page replaces the previous regional lgmsape...blob.core.windows.net entries with a larger list of amsu...lmsas.blob.core.windows.net endpoints. Administrators managing outbound firewall or allowlist rules should review the new list to support Windows Autopilot diagnostics uploads.

View all updates for 7 August 2026 →

item.title: Service release 2607 adds Samsung Knox E-FOTA management for corporate Android — 30 July 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 30 July 2026

Service release 2607 adds Samsung Knox E-FOTA management for corporate Android

The substantive change is a new Intune integration with Samsung Knox E-FOTA in the week of July 27, 2026 service release 2607. The same release documentation adds Windows settings-catalog coverage and seven Microsoft Edge policy settings. Microsoft Tunnel updates are operational: one records a July 27 image release and another changes the documented Ubuntu host version. The remaining edits are largely editorial: the archive backfills earlier announcements, while the Azure Virtual Desktop page clarifies its Azure subscription and Entra ID relationship. No retirement, security advisory, or explicit GA designation appears in the supplied evidence.

Intune · General

Samsung Knox E-FOTA enters the current Intune service-release documentation

The Intune What's new entry says Intune now integrates with Samsung Knox E-FOTA, allowing administrators to control the firmware version assigned to each device, deploy updates without user interaction, and schedule downloads and installations. It applies to Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated (COSU), fully managed (COBO), and corporate-owned with a work profile (COPE) devices. The evidence identifies this as a service release 2607 addition but does not explicitly label it GA.

Intune · General

Windows settings catalog adds camera, Keyboard Filter, and WSL options

New settings cover camera behavior, Keyboard Filter controls for Windows Insider devices, and Windows Subsystem for Linux. The documented path is Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog, and the entry applies to Windows 10 and Windows 11.

Intune · General

Edge administrative templates refresh to version 149

The templates were refreshed to Microsoft Edge 149, version 149.0.4022.21, adding the latest Edge 148 and 149 policy settings. The named additions cover Local Fonts allow and block URL lists, M365 authentication popups in work profiles, MAM enrollment when Purview DLP is configured on the managed device, automatic Copilot contextual-insights panes for Outlook links, and Browsing with Copilot allow and block URL lists.

Intune · Device security

Microsoft Tunnel upgrade notes record version 20260624.1

The July 27, 2026 Tunnel release entry records version 20260624.1, agent image digest sha256:9a7316aaea439dd634b7e073dccc44977e2bb8cdbbf3245cc6288b7932334721, and server image digest sha256:fa286ab658830ded388d839b17420c13cf7fb076f806701d76d7e6867f83859b. The listed changes are minor bug fixes; no new Tunnel capability is described.

Intune · Device security

Microsoft Tunnel prerequisites now list Ubuntu 26.04 with Docker CE

The prerequisites table replaces the Ubuntu 22.04 and Docker CE row with Ubuntu 26.04 and Docker CE. This is a documentation change to the stated host prerequisite; the supplied diff does not say that existing Ubuntu 22.04 deployments are retired or that an immediate upgrade is mandatory.

item.title: Configuration Manager’s SQL Server guidance now separates versions from required settings — 29 July 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 29 July 2026

Configuration Manager’s SQL Server guidance now separates versions from required settings

The main development is a Configuration Manager documentation split, not a product feature launch. A new Supported configurations for SQL Server article now contains required and optional settings, while the existing versions article focuses on supported versions, editions, and compatibility levels. Related installation, prerequisite, international-support, database-replica, and LTSB links now point to the separated guidance. The other edits are largely mechanical: CVE-2026-47301 links lose the /en-US path, and a boundary-group procedure corrects “CGM SUP” to “CMG SUP.” Separately, an Intune Message Center notice recommends Windows KB5101684 Preview for full remediation of IT1431577.

Configuration Manager · General

New article centralizes Configuration Manager SQL Server requirements

The new reference article applies to Configuration Manager current branch and SQL Server installations used for site databases, including SQL Server Express. It specifies SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS for the SQL Server instance and site database, Windows authentication, and memory guidance: 50–80 percent of addressable system memory when SQL Server shares the site-server computer, 80–90 percent on a dedicated remote database server, with minimum buffer-pool reserves of 8 GB for central administration and primaryب?

Configuration Manager · General

Version guidance now covers editions and compatibility levels separately

The updated Supported SQL Server versions article now covers supported versions, editions, and compatibility levels, while linking required settings to the new article. It also clarifies that only Database Engine Services is required, SQL Server replication is needed for database replicas for management points but not ordinary Configuration Manager database replication, and site databases require 64-bit SQL Server on a dedicated named or default instance.

Intune · Windows

Windows KB5101684 Preview is recommended for IT1431577 remediation

An Intune Message Center notice recommends installing Windows cumulative update KB5101684 Preview to fully remediate the issue tracked as IT1431577. The notice describes a client fix and platform improvements; it is a preview-update recommendation, not a general-availability Intune feature announcement.

item.description:

item.description:
Day in brief · 24 July 2026

Samsung Knox E-FOTA guidance highlights firmware campaigns, targeting performance, and EPM scope tags

This was a documentation-led period with two new Intune articles and 18 updates, but no Message Center notices or retirements. The most substantive additions document Samsung Knox E-FOTA integration prerequisites and capabilities, introduce a broader targeting-method framework, warn against inefficient dynamic-group rules, and record an Endpoint Privilege Management scope-tag limitation. Other changes mainly clarify navigation, external links, dates, and related content; the new Samsung article does not by itself establish a separate preview or general-availability announcement.

Intune · Endpoint analytics

Samsung Knox E-FOTA integration gets a new Intune setup article

The new how-to documents an integration that, according to the article, can launch, manage, and monitor Samsung firmware campaigns from the Intune admin center; lock devices to an OS version or selected firmware; and schedule download and installation windows. It says deployments require a Samsung Knox E-FOTA license and at least Microsoft 365 E3, support Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated, fully managed, and COPE enrollment types, and require an Intune Administrator plus a Samsung Knox administrator for-

Intune · Device enrollment

A new guide separates group scope from Intune policy targeting

The new targeting guide recommends starting with a broad audience and refining it with assignment filters, rather than creating many policy-specific groups. It distinguishes groups, which define the audience, from filters, which determine which devices in that audience receive a policy, and says group membership is processed when identity attributes change while filters evaluate at each device check-in. This is targeting guidance, not evidence of a new targeting behavior.

Intune · Fundamentals

Intune guidance says to avoid memberOf in dynamic group rules

The performance guidance now explicitly says not to use the memberOf operator in dynamic group rules. It recommends direct comparisons such as -eq, -startsWith, and -in, explaining that transitive membership lookups can add significant processing complexity and, in large environments, lead to long evaluation times or unexpected results. Where possible, it suggests using a direct device property or an assignment filter instead.

Endpoint Privilege Management · Windows

EPM scope tags remain unsupported by two documented roles

The known-issues page states that the built-in Endpoint Privilege Manager role and the custom Endpoint Privilege Management Policy Authoring role do not support scope tags. The documented workaround for restricting an administrator's view with scope tags is to grant permissions that include Read for Device configurations.

Intune · Device enrollment

Apple token procedures now use the Apple enrollment tab

The token-management procedure replaces the Intune Apple mobile tab with the Apple tab. For renewal, it now directs administrators to Apple Business's Devices and Management Services areas, or Apple School Manager's Preferences and Your MDM servers areas, then to the relevant service or server and Download Token; in Apple Business, Download Token is under the top-right Actions menu. This is a procedural and terminology clarification rather than evidence of a product behavior change.

item.title: Configuration Manager software update scans separate cache reuse from WSUS connectivity — 19 July 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 19 July 2026

Configuration Manager software update scans separate cache reuse from WSUS connectivity

The period contains a substantive clarification to Configuration Manager Software Updates guidance. It separates the forced/non-forced decision, which controls cache reuse, from the online/offline decision, which controls whether a scan obtains metadata from WSUS or local storage. This is documentation clarification, not evidence of a new feature, preview, general availability change, retirement, or changed product behavior.

Configuration Manager · Compliance

Forced scans ignore the cached compliance results

A non-forced scan reuses the last scan results while they remain current and within the TTL, running a new scan only when the cache is stale. A forced scan always runs a new scan and ignores the cache.

Configuration Manager · General

Online and offline scans use different metadata sources

For a scan that actually runs, online mode connects to WSUS on the software update point to refresh metadata. Offline mode evaluates the client with metadata already stored locally and does not connect to WSUS. An online scan therefore does not necessarily contact WSUS when a non-forced scan can use current cached results.

Configuration Manager · Compliance

One scan evaluates the entire synchronized update catalog

A scan evaluates all update metadata synchronized on the software update point, including updates in new deployments, existing deployments, and no deployments. Targeting a client with 1 deployment or 10 deployments does not change the number of scans.

item.description:
Day in brief · 2 July 2026

Android BYOD web enrollment guidance flags an irreversible tenant-level setting

The period was largely maintenance, but the substantive Intune changes center on Android Enterprise personally owned work-profile enrollment and forthcoming device-management capabilities. Updated guidance centers a single enrollment profile for web and Company Portal flows, while clarifying that web enrollment is tenant-level and irreversible and may conflict with device-bound phone-call MFA. Intune’s in-development page also adds Samsung Knox E-FOTA integration and Windows registry and app-inventory work. The macOS token procedure was broadened to cover both Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager; this is a procedural clarification, not a feature launch.

Intune · Device enrollment

Android BYOD guidance centers one profile for web and app enrollment

The setup article now says admins first create an enrollment profile that supports both web-based and Company Portal app-based enrollment. Web enrollment is enabled as an additional step by selecting Use web enrollment for all users enrolling into Android personally owned work profile management; when passkeys are the only authentication method, the guidance says to leave it unselected and use Company Portal enrollment instead.

Intune · Device enrollment

Web enrollment is documented as tenant-level and irreversible

The revised setup guidance explicitly states that enabling web-based enrollment applies at the tenant level and cannot be reversed. This clarifies the scope and consequence of the setting rather than announcing a product-behavior change.

Intune · Device enrollment

Phone-call MFA might break Android web enrollment

The updated guidance records a limitation: if MFA requires a phone call that the user must answer on the device being enrolled, web enrollment might break. It lists authenticating on a secondary device or using SMS as workarounds and says the limitation will be resolved in a future update, without providing a date.

Intune · General

Samsung firmware control and Windows fleet visibility enter the roadmap

The In development page adds an upcoming Knox E-FOTA integration that would surface remote firmware deployment in the Intune admin center for eligible corporate-owned Samsung Android Enterprise devices: dedicated (COSU), fully managed (COBO), and corporate-owned with a work profile (COPE). It also lists Windows properties-catalog collection of HKLM registry data through Single Value, All Values Under Key (Non-Recursive), or Same Value Across Subkeys, plus Advanced Analytics multi-device Windows app-inventory querys

Intune · Device enrollment

macOS token instructions now separate Apple Business and School Manager paths

The enrollment program token procedure now explicitly covers Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager with portal-specific steps. It changes the Intune action label from Add to Create and explains that Apple Business Manager creates a device management service while Apple School Manager creates an MDM server; both processes produce a server token uploaded to Intune. This is a procedure clarification, not evidence of a new token capability.

Intune · General

item.title: Remote Help guidance tightens unattended-access warnings on recording and sensitive work — 26 June 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 26 June 2026

Remote Help guidance tightens unattended-access warnings on recording and sensitive work

The period contained two Remote Help documentation updates, both focused on security guidance for unattended access. The edits strengthen the wording from recommendations to IMPORTANT guidance, but provide no evidence of a product-behavior change, new feature, or availability change.

Remote Help · Android

Deploy guidance prohibits screen-recording and mirroring apps

The Remote Help Deploy page changes the notice from a recommendation not to install or allowlist screen-recording or mirroring apps to IMPORTANT guidance: on devices using unattended access, do not install or allowlist any apps that can record or mirror the screen. It also recommends avoiding sensitive operations during unattended control sessions. This is a documentation and security-guidance clarification, not evidence of an enforced product control.

Remote Help · General

Start Session guidance makes sensitive operations explicitly disallowed

The Remote Help Start Session page changes its advice from limiting activity to nonsensitive operations to IMPORTANT guidance that operators must not perform sensitive operations during an unattended control session, even when the device screen is blocked to the end user. It repeats the prohibition on apps that can record or mirror the screen.

item.title: Intune plans iOS 18 and macOS 15 minimums later this year — 25 June 2026
item.description:
Day in brief · 25 June 2026

Intune plans iOS 18 and macOS 15 minimums later this year

The period is dominated by two future Apple platform support changes and three targeted documentation updates. Intune will raise its iOS/iPadOS and macOS support floors later this year; the documentation also records an Android app version requirement, an Android BYOD enrollment limitation, and revised macOS PKG update guidance. No new feature launch is evidenced in this set.

Intune · App management

iOS/iPadOS 18 becomes the planned minimum after Apple’s iOS 27 release

A Message Center plan-for-change notice says Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or higher after Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27 later this year. Administrators should check device compatibility and Intune reports; userless devices enrolled through ADE have different OS requirements.

Intune · Device enrollment

macOS 15 will be required for new enrollments after macOS 27

After Apple’s macOS Golden Gate 27 release, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Devices already enrolled on macOS 14.x or earlier remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will be blocked. Identify and upgrade affected devices before the change.

Intune · Android

Android Intune app support now starts at version 2025.11.01

The updated guidance says the minimum supported Microsoft Intune app for Android is version 2025.11.01, effective May 1, 2026; older versions might cause sign-in failures. Administrators can use Apps > Monitor > Discovered apps to find affected devices, while most users should receive updates automatically.

Intune · Device enrollment

Personally owned blocking is limited for AMAPI and newer Custom DPC devices

The Android personal work profile guidance now warns that setting Personally owned to Block does not apply to Android Management API devices and is not reliable for Android 12 and later devices using Custom DPC enrollment. It documents corporate-owned work profiles or group-based enrollment restrictions as alternatives.

Intune · App management

macOS available PKG updates are documented as automatic

The updated unmanaged PKG guidance now states that uploading a new version of an available app does not require users to select Install or Reinstall in Company Portal; the app installs automatically. This is a documentation-level correction to deployment expectations, not evidence of a newly announced feature.
